label: POINT IN TIME REPLAY (backtest), not live paper trading
method: Every deposit of $500k or more of LINK, UNI, PEPE or SHIB into an exchange hub in the window, replayed at the next hourly pass with chain state, prices and volume available at that time. Live gates unchanged. Decisions were hash chained in data/backtest/supply-decisions.jsonl before any outcome was fetched. Spread uses the live book at replay time as a proxy.

detail.why: Block size is immaterial against UNI's deep liquidity: modeled 0.6% move is under one-tenth of daily volatility, so realised PnL would be dominated by noise rather than the flow. Provenance is also unestablished — a single-transaction wallet forwarding its entire balance through a deposit address is as likely to be custody/OTC settlement as it is a seller. Both the size test and the intent test fail.

Supply-to-exchange is plausible but unproven: a 4-transaction EOA forwarding its entire balance through an intermediary deposit address is as likely a custody hop or OTC leg as a liquidation. Even if sold, $7.6M into $447M daily volume moves LINK less than one-eighth of a daily sigma, so the modeled edge is dominated by ordinary price noise. Size and identity both fail the bar; stand down.

Depositor profile supports real supply, but the block is too small relative to SHIB liquidity to move price reliably; modeled edge is a fraction of daily volatility and the market has just moved up ~1%, so any short is a coin flip on noise rather than on the flow.

Exchange-to-exchange internal movement fails the supply test: no beneficial owner is liquidating. Modeled 0.87% impact also sits barely above the 0.38% edge floor against 4.1% daily sigma and $513M volume, so even a genuine block would be noise-dominated. Market has not moved, consistent with participants reading this as an internal transfer.

Supply signal is weak: small share of balance sent, tiny share of supply, high-frequency wallet consistent with market making or routine flow. Impact math (0.94%) barely clears the 0.39% edge floor and is dwarfed by daily volatility, while price has already moved +4.8% in the last two hours against a short entry. Risk of shorting into strength for a sub-sigma edge is not justified.

Not real sellable supply: 245k-tx non-contract address behaving as a conduit, 0.036% of supply, negligible modeled impact (0.445%) versus an already +8% two-hour move which is the wrong direction for a short entry anyway. No causal path from this deposit to a price decline.
